about: The country workshops (Docs/Design/72-pulling-the-country-into-the-world.md, 4.6 and the Siting's Phase 5 rows; doc 71, 5): real businesses in the communities, each at the map's fixed building id (`building`, an interior; its keeper's flat `<building>_flat`, or the community's flat `for` its name), merged into its community's market (communities.json: the map's entry for the building gives its work spots, else `work` here). Their posts are staffed as the communities' markets are (farm_people.json `market`: the keeper of the towns' trades and shops, then those who keep the house, then service and labour, the post's words first; the hands of those who keep the house first), when the community's first farm or works is, the keeper living in the flat, the hands in the community's cottages; nobody is made. Each is a business of businesses.json (`business`: its crafts in crafts.json, its wares what they make) with a till of its own, its posts paid as a city maker's are (the till's keeper's and hands' wages, which follow its takings: the rule wageDrift), and owned by `house` (doc 42, Phase 5b: a workshop is a House's, which takes all the profit): what its till holds each night over its float and floatWagesDays of its wages goes to that House's estate (the Country's purse, the Houses' estates and the sea trade, booked by House with the works' rents). The House is the land's: Coldwater's and Larkfield's the Crown's (its herds' and grain farms'), the potteries Greatly's (by its clay pits: House Greatly is construction, doc 67 R25), Oakhaven's Timberland's (the woods'). They sell to the city's shops till to till (country.json `suppliers`, the resale path: at the store room's price, no toll, no carriage) and to any household whose own community's shops lack their goods; the store room supplies only what they lack. Crews sized to their inputs and to what the Country sold of their goods in country4's year 3 (the doc's ~29 was doc 71's plausible count before the inputs were known). A world without a building (build 60's export) has none of its workshop: its goods stay the store room's.

workshops.name: Coldwater Soapworks
workshops.about: Fine soap and tallow candles of the herds' tallow (piling at the farms), herbs from the marsh, cord from the chandlery and the ropewalk: soap ~43 crew-hours a day for the ~21 the Country sold, candles ~23 for the ~80 a day the shops went short of.

workshops.name: Coldwater Looms
workshops.about: Wool scarves of the two sheep runs' wool (~12 a day, ~10 of it piling): ~19 crew-hours a day.

workshops.name: Larkfield Looms
workshops.about: Linen of the grain farms' flax: the ~5 a day the store room still sold beside the city's weaver, and the presses' paper (~4 more).

workshops.name: Larkfield Print House
workshops.about: Pamphlets and paper (the Country sold ~19 pamphlets and ~4 paper a day): with Oakhaven's, ~60 crew-hours a day.

workshops.name: Larkfield Smithy
workshops.about: Iron hoops (beside the smithies and the cooperage), nails and cookpots, of the Country's iron bars: a smith's work and a half.

workshops.name: Fenshore Kilns
workshops.about: Clay pots of the Mirebridge pit's clay (the Country sold ~34 pots a day: ~27 crew-hours for the two potteries). A potter alone: a pot sold on at the store room's price leaves ~1.2p an hour over its clay, about one wolf's wage for half the pots; a hand would stand idle on the other's (the kiln hand's rule is there for later).

workshops.name: Southmeadow Kilns
workshops.about: Clay pots of the Fens pit's clay.

workshops.name: Oakhaven Print House
workshops.about: Pamphlets and paper, the press nearer the city.
